translationRepairs: With Chen Chi he stormed Dongguan, took it, and received brevet provincial commander rank.
With Chen Shi he stormed Dongguan, took it, and received brevet provincial commander rank.
The name 陳湜 is Chen Shi; Chi does not match the reading Shí already preserved in the extraction's pinyin.
He again joined Chen Chi in attacking Dongguan, took it, and was given the brevet rank of provincial military commander.
He again joined Chen Shi in attacking Dongguan, took it, and was given the brevet rank of provincial military commander.
The paired literal field contains the same incorrect reading of 陳湜 and must use Chen Shi.
In the fourth month they jointly assaulted Jingzhuguan: Li Chaobin on the upper river, Yisheng on the lower. The rebels were pinned by the fleet and could not look inland.
In the fourth month they jointly assaulted Jinzhu Pass: Li Chaobin on the upper river, Yisheng on the lower. The rebels were pinned by the fleet and could not look inland.
金柱關 is Jinzhu Pass; Jingzhuguan misreads 金 and redundantly retains guan after translating it as Pass.
He garrisoned Huangshiji, struck Wuhu rebels, and fought at Pangji, Yinjahui, and Zongyang with distinction, earning promotion to coordinator.
He garrisoned Huangshiji, struck Wuhu rebels, and fought at Xiaoji, Yinjiahui, and Zongyang with distinction, earning promotion to coordinator.
蟂 is read xiao, so the place is Xiaoji, not Pangji or the proposal's Xianji; 殷家匯 is Yinjiahui.
The forward mobile commander was posted to Hankou and the rear mobile commander to Liumen.
The forward mobile commander was posted to Hongkou and the rear mobile commander to Liumen.
The source has 谾口, not 漢口; Hongkou follows the reading of 谾 and avoids inventing Hankou.

Pressing Huzhou from Jiapu on Changxing, he faced tens of thousands of rebels fortifying the hills; while Yang Dingxun and Liu Shiji held the front, Chaobin landed his sailors on the rear in a pincer and destroyed every northwest river fort.

Pressing Huzhou from Jiapu toward Changxing, he faced tens of thousands of rebels fortifying the hills; while Yang Dingxun and Liu Shiji held the front, Chaobin landed his sailors on the rear in a pincer and destroyed every northwest river fort.
由夾浦逼長興 means advancing from Jiapu to press Changxing; 'on Changxing' is not idiomatic or syntactically accurate.
At Tianjiazhen he led ten boats in a forty-li chase, destroyed rebel shipping, and was raised to coordinator.
At Tianjiazhen he led ten boats in a chase of more than forty li, destroyed rebel shipping, and was raised to coordinator.
四十餘里 means more than forty li, so the idiomatic field should retain 餘.
